thread.title: Intraday Update: It’s Always Calm Before a Stock Storm - Barron's

author: Brett Arends
title: Intraday Update: It’s Always Calm Before a Stock Storm - Barron's
text:
By Brett Arends May 2, 2018 1:08 p.m. ET Markets were treading water Wednesday morning as investors kept their eyes on the Federal Reserve, whose latest rate-setting meeting ends today.
Illustration: Bloomberg News The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down about 60 points by midday, while the Standard & Poor’s 500 was off 0.25% and the Nasdaq Composite down 0.1%. The Russell 2000 small-cap index was about half a percent in the black. Advancers and decliners were roughly even. Treasury yields were holding steady, with the 10-year hovering around 2.97%.
Apple (AAPL) jumped 4% in the wake of Tuesday evening’s quarterly results. It beat forecasts, as it usually does, and bumped up its cash return to stockholders through buybacks and dividends. CEO Tim Cook denied that sales of the flagship $999 iPhone X have been a disappointment. However, the financials show that the average price of an iPhone, which was about $800 in the Christmas quarter, fell almost 10% to $728 in the following three months. Make of that what you will.
Tesla (TSLA) was up 0.2% despite news it is being sued for $2 billion for alleged patent infringements.
Facebook (FB) rose 1.4% after Mark Zuckerberg announced plans to compete with Tinder by launching a dating app. A cynic might say: Just think of the extra data they could sell the Russians!
Snap (SNAP) is in chaos. It’s down 20% after poor earnings. CNBC’s Jim Cramer says the earnings call was like a Saturday Night Live parody. Awkward data point: It is now a third below the $17 price of its IPO just over a year ago.
Among other widely-followed stocks, Amazon.com (AMZN) was off 0.6%, Alphabet-aka-Google (GOOGL) was down 0.7%, and Netflix (NFLX) was about even.
Meanwhile, watch out for “King Dollar.” The greenback kept edging up, with the U.S. Dollar Index rising another 0.23%. The dollar nudged 0.84 euros, 0.74 British pounds, 110 Japanese yen, and parity with the Swiss franc. Bespoke Investment Group points out the Dollar Index just broke above its 200-day moving average. That’s a technical indicator that may matter simply if enough people think it does.
The dollar has now risen about 3% since the president tapped Larry Kudlow, an Expensive Dollar fan, as his chief economic adviser. Kudlow refers to an expensive dollar as “King Dollar.” Didn’t FDR say something once about “economic royalists”?
An expensive dollar should reduce inflation and be good for bondholders. But it is a headwind for the real economy. Standard economic math says a more expensive currency makes it harder for U.S. businesses to compete with overseas rivals. It was no coincidence China artificially cheapened its currency for years while hollowing out the U.S. manufacturing base.
The good news? If the dollar keeps rising, coastal elitists will save a ton of money on their summer vacations in Europe.
Midday Movers Alcoa (AA) is up 1.8% to $52.93 after Jefferies initiated coverage of the stock with a Buy rating.
Aptiv (APTV) is up 6.5% to $90.02 after reporting first-quarter earnings . The vehicle components maker earned $1.29 a share on revenue of $3.63 billion, while analysts were looking for earnings of $1.19 a share on revenue of $3.35 billion. For the full year, it expects to earn $5.20 to $5.40 a share, compared with the $5.20 per-share consensus estimate. "Aptiv reported a strong start to the year; beating guidance, raising its 2018 outlook, and continuing the strong bookings seen in 2017," writes Cowen analyst Jeffrey Osborne. "We continue to be impressed by the company's position in Active Safety and High Voltage Electrification, where sales grew 57% and 64% respectively y/y in 1Q."
Humana (HUM) is down 2.8% to $287 after reporting first-quarter earnings . The health insurer earned $3.36 a share, compared with the $3.20 per-share consensus. For the full year, it expects to earn between $13.70 and $14.10 a share, compared with the $13.87 analysts are expecting.
T-Mobile US (TMUS) is down 1.8% to $58.35 after reporting first-quarter earnings . The wireless carrier earned 78 cents a share on revenue of $10.5 billion. Analysts were looking for 70 cents a share on revenue of $10.38 billion. It added 1.4 million net subscribers in the quarter.
Unum Group (UNM) is down 15.9% to $40.29 after reporting first-quarter earnings . The insurer earned $1.24 a share on revenue of $2.9 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of $1.25 a share on revenue of $2.89 billion. — Teresa Rivas
